identity.title: The Extraordinary Outburst in the Massive Protostellar System NGC 6334I-MM1: Flaring of the Water Masers in a North-South Bipolar Outflow Driven by MM1B

paper_type_evidence.quote: We compare multi-epoch sub-arcsecond VLA imaging of the 22 GHz water masers toward the massive protocluster NGC 6334I observed before and after the recent outburst of MM1B in (sub)millimeter continuum.
ALMA images of CS (6-5) reveal a highly-collimated north-south structure encompassing the flaring masers to the north and the non-flaring masers to the south

findings_qualitative.value: Water masers near MM1 weakened while CM2 masers flared, forming a bow shock pointing back to MM1B

evidence.quote: Since the outburst, the water maser emission toward MM1 has substantially weakened.

claims.hypothesis: Flaring CM2 water masers trace the interaction of an MM1B outflow with ambient gas
claims.experiment: Three-epoch VLA water maser imaging and ALMA CS (6-5) imaging
claims.result: Bow shock pattern with vertex at CM2; N-S CS outflow encompassing masers
claims.finding: Masers trace the MM1B N-S outflow; radiative energy of outburst strengthened northern masers

evidence.quote: We conclude that CM2, the water masers, and many of the excited OH masers trace the interaction of the high velocity bipolar outflow from MM1B with ambient molecular gas.

claims.hypothesis: Southern water masers show bulk motion away from MM1B

evidence.quote: Proper motions of the southern water masers over 5.3 years indicate a bulk projected motion of 117 km s$^{-1}$ southward from MM1B with a dynamical time of 170 yr.

claims.hypothesis: Outburst dust heating reduces water maser pumping near MM1
claims.result: MM1 masers faded by factors of 5 to 16
claims.finding: Attributed to increased dust temperature reducing pump efficiency

evidence.quote: faded substantially, by factors of 5 to 16, while some velocity components have disappeared entirely, which we attribute to the increased dust temperature reducing the efficiency of the maser pump

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: NGC 6334I-South maser might be associated with star TPR-9 outflow or pumped by beamed MM1B radiation; cannot exclude

evidence.quote: we cannot exclude the possibility that this maser was somehow pumped by narrowly beamed radiation from MM1B
